symptom: Every exec of the script defining a database connection rewrote its Queries list marker from 3 to 2 (exec reported Modified on a connection nothing had changed), and the next Studio Pro save set it back to 3: a version-control diff on every round trip. mx check, lint and the build were clean
cause: db_write.go registered Queries as marker 2 (MandatoryListMarkers for the empty list, a DatabaseQuery child-type marker for the populated one). The 2 came from the legacy serializer's initial commit (`bson.A{int32(2)} // versioned array prefix` for every list in the tree), never from a measurement; the port to modelsdk copied it field-for-field
fix: Register DatabaseConnection.Queries as an owner/key mandatory property list with marker 3 (RegisterMandatoryPropertyList), so it covers empty and populated lists and canon.NormalizeListMarkers moves a stale stored 2 to 3; the child-type DatabaseQuery marker to 3. AdditionalProperties, Parameters, TableMappings and Columns stay 2
insight: Within one document Studio Pro mixes markers: Queries is 3 while every list below it and AdditionalProperties beside it are 2, so 'the legacy writer used one marker for the whole tree' is a sign the value was never measured. A same-version `mx convert --in-place -s` on a copy of a blank project is a cheap Studio Pro stand-in for a doctype the fixtures lack: it re-serializes every unit, and an empty-list and a populated-list instance in one run settle whether the marker depends on emptiness (here it does not). Compare decoded trees sorted per path: Studio Pro also reorders keys alphabetically, which is not a semantic difference
